newsitem.title: USA: TENNIS-HURTING MARTINEZ SURVIVES AT CHASE CHAMPIONSHIPS.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-HURTING MARTINEZ SURVIVES AT CHASE CHAMPIONSHIPS.

text.p: Former Wimbledon champion Conchita Martinez overcame a sore left hamstring and an unexpectedly stiff challenge from the lowest-ranked player in the field, Judith Wiesner, to advance at the season-ending Chase Championships Wednesday.

Although she needed treatment by the trainer after the second set, the fourth-seeded Martinez moved easily and comfortably around the court in the final set to complete a 6-1 3-6 6-4 opening-round win in the $2 million tournament at Madison Squre Garden.
Martinez, whose only Grand Slam singles title came at Wimbledon in 1994, felt her leg stiffen up late in the second set against the Austrian, ranked 19th in the world.
"I hurt it about three days ago and suddenly it felt worse," Martinez said of the injury.
Martinez felt a little bit better after taking a 4-1 lead in the last set before Wiesner rallied to take the next three games.
But the Spaniard wrapped up the one hour and 59 minute struggle in the next two games, losing just three points.
The hard-fought win put Martinez into the quarter-finals of the season-ending tournament for the fifth year in a row.

Martinez, 24, will not have much time to rest. She is scheduled back on the court Thursday against Iva Majoli, the Croatian teenager who upset last year's runner-up Anke Huber of Germany on opening night.

The 30-year-old Wiesner, the oldest player in the elite 16-player field, was making only her second appearance in the event. She suffered a first-round loss in 1990 and seemed destined to make another quick exit after losing the first set in 30 minutes.
Wiesner started her comeback by breaking Martinez for a 3-1 second-set lead. After the two traded service breaks in the next two games, Wiesner held for a 5-2 lead.
"I was playing more aggressive and serving better," Wiesner said of the second set when she had 15 winners and lost just six points on her first serve.
The Austrian evened the match when Martinez whistled a bakchand passing shots just wide on the fourth set point.
Martinez and Wiesner were playing for the first time in three years, but little had changed with the passage of time as the Spaniard won for the seventh time in a row.
"We both play from the baseline and she is just more consistent," Wiesner said.
